sourceInformation.source: Ice Hockey (Activision, Atari 2600, 1981), designed by Alan Miller
sourceInformation.perspective: 3D fixed elevated broadcast view; optional overhead camera
sourceInformation.tech: Three.js 0.180.0 (R180), WebGPURenderer: WebGPU on hardware adapters, WebGL2 compatibility for unavailable or known software adapters; Rapier 3D compat 0.19.3; Gamepad API; Web Audio API; PeerJS 1.5.5; AI Hub session client 1.4.0 / protocol v1; HTML/CSS/JavaScript
sourceInformation.artDirection: Procedural cel-shaded geometry, ink outlines, scratched sea-glass ice, cream, teal and coral coastal arena
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer and AnimationClip keyframe tracks for skating, stick swings and celebrations; procedural leaning, falling, particles and camera motion
sourceInformation.audio: Code-generated synth music (10% default), synthesized hockey effects and formant-like Animalese/Simlish gibberish; no audio files
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub shared-world sessions for 1–4 players; standalone 1v1 WebRTC rooms via PeerJS signaling, same-origin BroadcastChannel transport for local windows; local two-player versus
sourceInformation.testing: Allowed: headless scripted full playthroughs, emulated gamepads and touch, two-page multiplayer, official AI Hub harness, Web Audio analysis and visual screenshots, with no FPS target. Hardware WebGPU appearance and physical-controller feel: unknown. Behavior through arbitrary remote NAT/firewalls: unknown.
sourceInformation.research: Original Activision instruction manual transcribed at AtariAge (mechanics, modes, stick timing, checking, zones and banks); archived Atari screenshots and packaging; official Three.js/Rapier documentation; AI Hub protocol and harness. Original pickup click confirmed; original music details unknown.
sourceInformation.environment: Codex CLI (headless); Linux / Ubuntu on WSL2

testingFeedback: 8 distinct issues across build checks, browser tests, visual inspection and input review; all corrected. Test-fixture timing problems are excluded.
3 were critical: a bundling syntax error, a Rapier startup API mismatch and a software WebGPU device loss that left the rink blank.

The two-page multiplayer playthrough: it verified host authority and score synchronization and exposed missing disconnect handling. The official AI Hub harness also verified four seats, packet loss, host departure and a server-only host.
Initial software-WebGPU screenshots were least helpful: the device was lost while the simulation continued. Renderer counters and compatibility-renderer screenshots made the result assessable.
engineFeedback: Three.js made a coherent procedural cel-shaded arena and native AnimationMixer clips straightforward to build and reuse.

Yes. I initially used the runtime rigid-body translation method on a Rapier descriptor, assumed ShapeGeometry UVs were normalized, and encountered a lost SwiftShader WebGPU device. Each was corrected or given a compatibility path.
The hockey rules, team AI, possession and 32-angle shot timing, controller menu navigation, touch assistance and host-authoritative multiplayer.
Coordinating fixed-step physics and snapshot playback while handling the supplied software WebGPU adapter losing its device.
More complete WebGPU device-loss recovery with an actionable fallback and clear documentation for switching backends.
promptFeedback: The concrete source, controller-first UX, mandatory attract mode and complete delivery contract gave the game a clear identity.
The source lacked a publisher/platform; I chose Activision’s Atari 2600 Ice Hockey from the title and year. Standalone online transport was also unspecified.
Finishing the hockey rules, six interactive drills, three-match Cup and four input paths while supporting standalone rooms and AI Hub in one shareable HTML file.
Specify the source publisher/platform and the intended standalone signaling service, relay or manual peer-exchange policy.

aiHub.name: Rink or Swim
aiHub.description: Two skaters. Three minutes. All heart. Bank shots, trade passes and throw cartoon checks in a coastal ink-and-ice arena, then chase the Breakwater Cup or challenge a friend.
aiHub.controls: Move: LS/WASD; aim: RS/mouse; hold/release Cross/Space/LMB to shoot; Square/E/RMB pass; Circle/Q check; Triangle/R switch; Options/Esc pause; touch: left drag skate, right drag aim/tap shoot.
